label: Amiata

names.text: "Asino dell'Amiata" taken from the Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch, where it is given as the Italian name. "Amiatina" is the article's own title (Amiatina), taken from its URL and heading.

about.text: A donkey breed from Tuscany, particularly associated with Monte Amiata in the provinces of Siena and Grosseto. It is used for transport, burden, light draught, meat and hippotherapy, and its jennies are milked for human consumption in a milk supply chain assessed for animal health and milk quality.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the Tuscan origin, the provinces, and the listed uses. Mad Barn research page, read on WebFetch: the milk chain for human consumption and the jennies as dairy animals.

origin.place: Monte Amiata in Tuscany, in the provinces of Siena and Grosseto; the article also notes populations in Liguria and Campania.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "particularly associated with Monte Amiata" in Siena and Grosseto, with populations in Liguria and Campania. The article gives no recognition or formation date, so none is used.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "2006: 1,082 registered, about 60% in Tuscany." A registered count, not a total population.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: uses listed as transport, burden, light draught, meat and hippotherapy. Mad Barn page, read on WebFetch: the jennies are dairy animals whose milk is assessed for human consumption, which places dairy first.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: FAO/DAD-IS risk status "endangered", listed in 2007. No current DAD-IS status was read directly.

facts.v: From 1956, the Deposito Stalloni (later the Istituto di Incremento Ippico) of Pisa selectively bred the breed in Grosseto.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the 1956 start and the Pisa institution, in the notable history section.

facts.v: The milk of the jennies is described as having high lactose, low casein and low fat, with more unsaturated fatty acids than ruminant milks, and high lysozyme activity compared with cow's milk. No numeric composition is given on the source page.

sources.text: Mad Barn research page, read on WebFetch: the qualitative description of the milk, as the page gives it.

gaps: No numeric milk composition or yield: the Mad Barn page gives none, and the figures seen in search text for a 28-jenny study were not traced to an opened page, so they are left out; the Mad Barn study year was not stated on the page; the Wikipedia article gives no recognition date; no current DAD-IS figure or risk status was read directly; a later count of about 2,300 seen in search text is from an unopened paper and is left out.
